readings.title: PHP2Shell: intelligence notes from this chat
readings.how: A research chat run by the editor in Perplexity on 22 October 2026, compiled by Perplexity into notes and given to this site by the editor. Perplexity read the web through search excerpts; it did not read the evidence vault.

rows.found: PHP2Shell names two PHP core vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619: a pair, not one CVE.
rows.vault: Confirmed from the CVE records, the GitHub advisories and php.net.

rows.found: W3Techs says PHP is used by 69.3% of all the websites 'whose server-side programming language we know'. Usage is not exposure: a site using PHP, running a flawed version, and being reachable through the flaw are three different populations.
rows.vault: The vault already carries the qualifier, second-hand: a security founder's post on X, captured on 22 October, says 'PHP runs 69% of websites whose server-side language is known'. The three pages that carry the bare 70% figure do not name the measurement. W3Techs itself is not captured; capturing it would make this first-hand and close the front page's open question.

rows.found: Wiz's own headline says 'affecting 70% of the Internet', so the broad wording is not only a journalist's paraphrase.
rows.vault: The same: the vault attributes '70% of the Internet' to Wiz's headline and X post, and marks it unverified.

rows.found: A BBC article attributes 'roughly 70%' to Wiz and says the BBC could not independently verify it.
rows.vault: The vault's capture of the BBC live page carries the same attribution. The BBC article Perplexity read is a different page and is not in the vault; it is listed below for capture.

rows.found: The per-CVE mechanisms (out-of-memory handling leaving request memory uninitialised; request state outliving its memory into the next request) are marked unverified, pending a primary advisory or a patch review.
rows.vault: Both mechanisms are stated in the CVE records and the GitHub advisories, and the fix commit was read from a clone of php-src. Perplexity's earlier descriptions were right; its caution was right too, given what it could read.

rows.found: 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27 and 8.5.12, treated as a collected lead because no official PHP advisory was retrieved.
rows.vault: Confirmed by php.net's advisory, the CVE records and the signed tags in php-src.

rows.found: Earlier answers said affected releases go back to PHP 5.4; not validated.
rows.vault: Disputed in the vault: Wiz says 5.4 and later, NCSC-NL from 5, CERT-FR lists 5.x to 8.1, while the CVE records list only 8.2 to 8.5; the project published backports down to 7.4.

rows.found: Demonstrations against WordPress, Drupal and Joomla; not validated.
rows.vault: Reported, not confirmed: Calif lists eleven applications and Wiz two, each by its own account; no third party has reproduced them in a captured source.

rows.found: A FAQ at php2shell.uk says the label began as the name of the researchers' combined exploit script. No earlier use of the name was found, which is not proof of first use.
rows.vault: The FAQ is not in the vault. What the vault holds fits it: on 20 October a screenshot of a 'PHP2Shell tool' credited to Calif.io circulated, per a PHP security team member's account, and the NSA calls the pair PHP2Shell.

rows.found: The collected evidence does not establish exploitation before disclosure; absence of evidence is not proof.
rows.vault: Amazon reports one exploit attempt against a honeypot on 17 October, four days before disclosure, from an anonymisation network. That is an attempt against a sensor, still not a compromise.

rows.found: Reports of exploitation attempts on 21 October are not proof of successful compromise.
rows.vault: The same, counted across every captured source: no named organisation has confirmed a compromise.

rows.found: Outstanding: a measured global exposure, rather than PHP's market share.
rows.vault: Open here too. The nearest are host counts: VulnCheck's 2.6 million internet-facing hosts and Censys's 1.57 million unpatched on 21 October, which count machines, not sites, and say nothing about configuration.

rows.found: The notes say that some technical details in Perplexity's earlier answers in the same chat were more specific than the excerpts it had retrieved could support, and mark them rather than repeat them.
rows.vault: This is the rule the verifier role exists to enforce here: a statement the captured text does not carry is downgraded, not repeated. A model applying it to itself is worth recording.
